9290418.headline: Limerick Council Clarifies Adare Access Rules Amid Ryder Cup Exclusion Concerns
9290418.summary: Limerick City and County Council has moved to address local worries following reports of a proposed two-kilometre exclusion zone in Adare during the upcoming Ryder Cup. Officials are working to clarify how access restrictions will impact residents and businesses during the major golf tournament.
9290418.story:
Limerick City and County Council has stepped in to clarify access restrictions in Adare ahead of the Ryder Cup, following mounting concern among local residents over a reported two-kilometre exclusion zone.

Reports of the proposed strict perimeter had raised anxieties within the community regarding how homeowners and local businesses would access their properties during the high-profile international golf competition.

Local representatives and council officials are now engaging with the community to address these concerns and provide definitive information on what traffic and security measures will actually be put in place for the event.
9290418.localAngle: This impacts local residents and businesses in Adare who are seeking clarity on how their daily lives and operations will be managed during the major international golf tournament.
9290418.originalTitle: Adare residents' concerns over Ryder Cup ‘2km exclusion zone’

9297190.headline: Caherdavin pupils show their colours for Na Piarsaigh ahead of county final
9297190.summary: Pupils at Christ the King in Caherdavin gathered to cheer on Na Piarsaigh ahead of the Limerick Senior Hurling Championship final.
9297190.story:
Excitement is building across the city as local schools throw their weight behind this weekend's sporting action. Pupils at Christ the King National School in Caherdavin paused their regular classes to show their support for Na Piarsaigh.

Students donned club jerseys and waved flags in the school yard to cheer on the team as they prepare for the Limerick Senior Hurling Championship final. The visit highlights the strong local ties between the Caherdavin school and the city hurling club.

With throw-in fast approaching, anticipation continues to mount among young fans and players alike across the 061 area as Na Piarsaigh looks ahead to the county showcase.
9297190.localAngle: The story highlights local school children in Caherdavin supporting a prominent Limerick GAA club ahead of the county hurling final.
9297190.originalTitle: PICTURES: Limerick school cheers on their team ahead of county final

9299281.headline: Castletroy Golf Club Member Laid to Rest Following Community Tributes
9299281.summary: A popular Limerick man and valued member of Castletroy Golf Club has been laid to rest following tributes remembering him as a kind and charming person.
9299281.story:
Family, friends, and members of the local sporting community gathered to pay their final respects to a popular Limerick man who has been laid to rest. 

Well-known within the local area, the deceased was widely regarded as a valued member of Castletroy Golf Club. Throughout his time with the club, he contributed significantly, dedicating both his time and talents to the community.

Those who knew him remembered him warmly following his passing, describing him as a lovely, kind, and charming person who left a lasting impression on fellow club members and the wider Limerick community.
9299281.localAngle: The man was a prominent and valued member of the Castletroy Golf Club in Limerick.
9299281.originalTitle: RIP: ’Such a lovely, kind, charming person’- Popular Limerick man is laid to rest

9300202.headline: All Seven Limerick Men's Rugby Teams Return to AIL Action This Weekend
9300202.summary: Limerick's seven men's rugby sides are back on the pitch this weekend following a two-week break as the 2026/27 season resumes.
9300202.story:
All seven of the Treaty County's Men’s sides will return to Energia All-Ireland League action this weekend following a two-week hiatus. The brief break comes to an end as the 2026/27 domestic rugby season begins to properly take shape across the divisions.

Clubs from across Limerick are preparing for their respective fixtures after the fortnight-long pause in the league schedule. The return of the AIL brings club rugby back to the forefront for local supporters and players alike.

Fixtures will kick off across various venues as the Limerick teams resume their campaigns. Coaches and squads have used the recent break to regroup ahead of a crucial block of matches in the league standings.
9300202.localAngle: All seven Limerick men's rugby sides are returning to action locally after a two-week break in the AIL season.
9300202.originalTitle: AIL action returns to Limerick following two-week hiatus

9300204.headline: Treaty United Women Host DLR Waves in 2026 Season Finale
9300204.summary: Treaty United Women conclude their 2026 SSE Airtricity Premier Division campaign this evening by hosting DLR Waves at 5pm.
9300204.story:
Treaty United Women will wrap up their 2026 SSE Airtricity Premier Division season on home turf this evening as they welcome DLR Waves to Limerick. Kick-off for the final fixture of the campaign is scheduled for 5pm.

The team enters the evening looking to finish their league season on a high note in front of home supporters at the Markets Field. Throughout the 2026 campaign, the squad has competed at the top tier of domestic women's football.

Tonight's match marks the final opportunity for fans to see the Treaty United side in action for the 2026 season. Both teams will be aiming to secure a positive result to close out their respective league campaigns.
9300204.localAngle: The fixture gives Limerick sports fans a final chance to support Treaty United Women on home ground as they conclude their 2026 Premier Division campaign.
9300204.originalTitle: Treaty United Women aim to finish season as history makers

9301758.headline: Woman Convicted at Kilmallock Court for Assaulting Garda at Bruff Station
9301758.summary: A woman has been convicted at Kilmallock District Court for assaulting a member of An Garda Síochána. The incident took place at Bruff garda station in County Limerick.
9301758.story:
A woman has been convicted following an incident where a member of An Garda Síochána was assaulted at Bruff garda station. The case was heard before Kilmallock District Court, where the details of the assault were presented to the judge.

The legal proceedings concluded with the court recording a conviction against the defendant for the attack on the Garda officer while at the County Limerick station.

Assaults on emergency service personnel continue to be treated with seriousness by the courts in Limerick and across the judicial system.
9301758.localAngle: The case was heard locally at Kilmallock District Court following an incident at Bruff garda station in County Limerick.
9301758.originalTitle: Conviction for woman who assaulted a garda in Limerick station

9302767.headline: Dromin-Athlacca and Bruff Clash in Premier Intermediate Hurling Final
9302767.summary: Dromin-Athlacca face neighbours Bruff this Sunday at the TUS Gaelic Grounds in the Lyons of Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship Final, aiming for an immediate return to the senior grade.
9302767.story:
Dromin-Athlacca are preparing for a crucial clash this Sunday as they face neighbouring rivals Bruff in the Lyons of Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship Final. 

The showdown is set to take place at the TUS Gaelic Grounds, where both sides will battle for the title and county bragging rights. 

Dromin-Athlacca enter the fixture hoping to secure an immediate return to the senior hurling grade at the very first attempt following their relegation.
9302767.localAngle: This high-stakes local derby brings together two Limerick communities at the TUS Gaelic Grounds for the county's Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship Final.
9302767.originalTitle: Dromin-Athlacca hoping to return to the senior grade at first attempt

9305835.headline: M9 Crash Survivors Ella, Niamh and Alma Share Heartfelt Message of Gratitude
9305835.summary: Three sisters critically injured in an August M9 crash that claimed five lives have issued a heartfelt message thanking supporters. They expressed that they are forever grateful for the care and support they received.
9305835.story:
Sisters Ella, Niamh and Alma, who were critically injured in a horror crash on the M9 in August, have shared a heartfelt message expressing that they are "forever grateful" for the support shown to them.

The devastating August collision resulted in the tragic deaths of five teenage boys. The three sisters sustained critical injuries during the incident.

In their message, the siblings reflected on their recovery and the overwhelming response they have received following the tragedy, offering their profound thanks as they continue to heal.
9305835.localAngle: The recovery of the three sisters resonates deeply across the region as local communities continue to offer support in the wake of the devastating M9 crash.
9305835.originalTitle: 'Forever grateful' -  Sisters injured in horror M9 crash share heartfelt message

9306638.headline: Limerick's Scarlett Faulkner Included in Special Prayers During Vatican Pilgrimage
9306638.summary: Siblings Scarlett and Jason Faulkner were specially remembered by family members during a pilgrimage to Italy, with prayers offered for Scarlett at the Vatican.
9306638.story:
Young Limerick siblings Scarlett and Jason Faulkner were placed at the forefront of their family's minds during a recent journey to Italy.

Family members on the pilgrimage ensured the siblings were remembered during their travels, culminating in special prayers offered for Scarlett at the Vatican.

The gesture brought a touch of Limerick to the heart of Vatican City as the family partook in the pilgrimage.
9306638.localAngle: The story connects local Limerick children Scarlett and Jason Faulkner to a high-profile pilgrimage and prayers offered at the Vatican in Rome.
9306638.originalTitle: Limerick’s Scarlett Faulkner prayed for at the Vatican

9307165.headline: Minister Patrick O'Donovan Speaks Out on Representation for People with Disabilities
9307165.summary: Limerick minister Patrick O'Donovan has spoken publicly about his desire to prove that individuals with disabilities or neurological conditions can successfully work in government.
9307165.story:
Minister Patrick O'Donovan has stated that he wants to demonstrate that people living with a disability or neurological condition can pursue and maintain careers in government. 

The Limerick-based minister made the remarks as he addressed the importance of visibility and inclusion for individuals facing these conditions within public service roles.

The intervention aims to challenge perceptions and show that public office and government work are accessible to all members of society, regardless of neurological or physical conditions.
9307165.localAngle: Limerick minister Patrick O'Donovan brings local representation to national government while advocating for greater inclusivity for people with disabilities.
9307165.originalTitle: EDITORIAL: 'Patrick O'Donovan has courage to speak out while others whisper'

9307466.headline: West Limerick Derby Set for Junior Hurling Championship Final Clash Today
9307466.summary: West Limerick rivals meet today in the Junior Hurling Championship final. Despite a 16-point margin when they last met two months ago, a tight contest is anticipated.
9307466.story:
Sports fans across the county are turning their attention to west Limerick today as two fierce local rivals collide in the Junior Hurling Championship final.

While previous encounters can often dictate expectations, supporters have been advised to pay no heed to the 16-point difference recorded when these two sides last met just two months ago. Instead, pundits and players alike are preparing for a much closer battle with the championship title officially on the line.

Throw-in brings an end to weeks of anticipation in the west division, where local pride and silverware are up for grabs. Both clubs will be looking to leave everything on the pitch as the championship reaches its thrilling conclusion.
9307466.localAngle: This high-stakes west Limerick hurling final brings together fierce local rivals to battle for divisional championship silverware.
9307466.originalTitle: Tasty west Limerick derby with Junior Hurling Championship on the line

9307472.headline: Doon Star Darragh Stapleton Named to Start Premier Junior Hurling Final
9307472.summary: Doon are preparing for the Premier Junior Hurling final with senior-experienced player Darragh Stapleton expected to anchor the attack at center forward. The crucial fixture takes place this weekend.
9307472.story:
Doon are aiming to go one better than their previous campaign as they ready themselves for the Premier Junior Hurling final. Preparations for the crucial fixture have been bolstered by the expected inclusion of Darragh Stapleton in the starting lineup.

Stapleton, who featured in last year’s Senior Hurling Championship final, is slated to line out at center forward for the side. His experience at the senior grade is expected to provide a significant boost as Doon look to secure the title.

The team enters the final with the clear objective of capturing the championship after falling just short in past efforts. Throw-in will see Stapleton and his teammates take to the field to claim the silverware.
9307472.localAngle: This match marks a major fixture for the local hurling community as Doon contend for the Premier Junior Hurling title.
9307472.originalTitle: Doon looking to go one better in Premier Junior Hurling final

9307476.headline: Bruree Targets Third Successive Limerick Intermediate Hurling Final Appearance
9307476.summary: South Limerick club Bruree are aiming for a breakthrough in the Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship final after suffering defeats at the final hurdle in each of the past two seasons.
9307476.story:
Bruree enter this year's Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship final determined to reverse their recent run of results. The south Limerick side has experienced consecutive heartbreak after falling at the final hurdle in each of the last two seasons.

With two successive final defeats weighing on the club, the team heads into the upcoming fixture hoping that this will finally be their year to secure the intermediate title. Both players and supporters will be looking to put the disappointment of previous campaigns behind them as they prepare for another shot at the championship.

The fixture marks a crucial moment for the south Limerick club as they attempt to break their losing streak on the county's hurling stage. Throw-in details and match preparations are currently underway across the parish.
9307476.localAngle: The match carries significant local interest across south Limerick as Bruree attempts to secure a long-awaited intermediate hurling title for the parish.
9307476.originalTitle: Bruree hoping to make it third time lucky in IHC final

9307685.headline: Limerick EuroMillions Player Wins €500,000 in Friday Night Draw
9307685.summary: A Limerick EuroMillions player is holding a winning ticket worth €500,000 following the latest draw. National Lottery officials have urged local ticket holders to check their numbers ahead of the Bank Holiday weekend.
9307685.story:
One lucky EuroMillions player in Limerick is celebrating an "incredible" win after capturing a €500,000 prize in the latest draw.

National Lottery spokesperson Emma Monaghan urged players in the county to check their slips carefully following Friday's draw, noting that a very exciting Bank Holiday weekend lies ahead for the unnamed winner.

Details regarding the exact location where the winning ticket was sold have not yet been released by National Lottery officials. Players across Limerick are being advised to sign the back of their tickets and contact National Lottery headquarters to arrange collection of the prize.
9307685.localAngle: The winning €500,000 EuroMillions ticket was purchased in Limerick, potentially setting up a local resident for a life-changing Bank Holiday weekend.
9307685.originalTitle: ‘Check your tickets carefully!’: Limerick player has ‘incredible’ EuroMillions win

9307767.headline: Limerick hurling star ties the knot with Elaine after meeting on night out
9307767.summary: Limerick wing-forward and six-time All-Ireland medalist has married his partner Elaine. The couple, who first met on a night out, received heartfelt best wishes on their wedding day.
9307767.story:
One of Limerick's most decorated hurlers has married his partner, Elaine, affectionately known as Lainey. The wing-forward, who boasts an impressive sporting resume including six All-Ireland medals and three All-Star awards, celebrated his wedding day surrounded by family and friends.

The couple's romance began on a traditional night out, leading up to their wedding day where they received heartfelt best wishes from supporters and well-wishers across the county.

While the hurling star is widely known for his exploits on the pitch and his collection of major GAA honours, the weekend belonged to the newlyweds as they marked the milestone event in their lives.
9307767.localAngle: The marriage of one of Limerick's most celebrated sports stars is a major talking point for local hurling fans across the 061.
9307767.originalTitle: Limerick hurling star receives heartfelt best wishes on his wedding day

9307849.headline: Monagea Claim Limerick Junior 'A' Hurling Title with Victory Over Killeedy
9307849.summary: Monagea secured an immediate return to the Premier Junior grade following a decisive win against Killeedy in the Limerick Junior 'A' hurling final.
9307849.story:
Monagea bounced straight back to the Premier Junior ‘A’ hurling ranks on Saturday, October 24, 2026, after proving too strong for Killeedy in the county final.

The victory marks a triumphant return for Monagea just one year after suffering relegation from the same grade. By overcoming Killeedy in Saturday's showdown, the club immediately reverses last season's setback and secures promotion back to the higher tier of Limerick hurling.

The county final result crowns a successful campaign for Monagea, who wasted no time in re-establishing their status following their drop down the divisions twelve months prior.
9307849.localAngle: This final decides the destination of the Limerick Junior 'A' hurling title and shapes the makeup of the county's hurling divisions for the upcoming season.
9307849.originalTitle: Monagea too strong for Killeedy in Limerick Junior 'A' hurling final

9307939.headline: Ben O’Connor’s Late Try Secures Bonus Point for Munster in Leinster Derby Defeat
9307939.summary: Munster secured a losing bonus point away to Leinster in the capital on Saturday evening, thanks to Ben O’Connor's late try despite spending most of the second half on the backfoot.
9307939.story:
Munster returned from the capital with a hard-fought losing bonus point on Saturday evening following a derby defeat to Leinster. Clayton McMillan’s side found themselves under immense pressure throughout the second half, spending virtually all of the period on the backfoot against their provincial rivals.

Despite the sustained territory and possession dominance from the hosts, Munster managed to salvage something from the fixture in the closing stages. A late try scored by Ben O’Connor proved crucial, ensuring the visitors did not leave empty-handed from the tough away encounter.

The late score salvaged a valuable bonus point for the squad in a demanding fixture, highlighting their persistence during a challenging second-half period where Leinster continually pressed the defensive line.
9307939.localAngle: This match carries significant interest for Limerick supporters following the fortunes of Munster Rugby in their high-profile inter-provincial rivalry.
9307939.originalTitle: Munster claim bonus point despite derby defeat to Leinster

9307944.headline: Knockaderry Defeat Bruree to Claim Historic Back-to-Back County Hurling Titles
9307944.summary: Knockaderry clinched the intermediate county title on Saturday, October 24, 2026, defeating Bruree despite entering the match as underdogs.
9307944.story:
Knockaderry pulled off a major upset on Saturday, October 24, 2026, defeating Bruree to capture the intermediate county hurling title.

Coming into the fixture widely regarded as the underdogs, Knockaderry rose to the occasion to secure a famous victory. The triumph marks a remarkable milestone for the club, adding intermediate honours to the Premier Junior crown they secured just 12 months prior.

The back-to-back county titles cement a dominant period for Knockaderry, who have successfully transitioned their winning momentum from their Premier Junior success last year straight into the intermediate ranks.
9307944.localAngle: This victory marks a major milestone for the Limerick club as they secure consecutive county titles following last year's Premier Junior success.
9307944.originalTitle: Knockaderry stun Bruree to secure back-to-back county titles

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.headline: Limerick Schools Rally Around Glenstal Abbey Following Shock Closure Announcement
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.summary: Local secondary schools have expressed solidarity with Glenstal Abbey after the shock announcement that the historic boarding school will close by August 2028. The 94-year-old institution cited a changing operating environment for its difficult decision to wind down operations.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.story:
Limerick secondary schools have spoken out in support of Glenstal Abbey following the shock announcement on October 23 that the school plans to close by August 2028. 

Villiers Secondary School on the North Circular Road released a statement on its website acknowledging the significance of the news for students, families, and staff. The school highlighted its long-standing relationship with Glenstal, noting their shared history with the Barrington family whose lands and buildings linked the two institutions. 

St. Munchin’s College on the Corbally Road also shared a statement of solidarity on Instagram, extending heartfelt thoughts to the entire Glenstal community, past pupils, parents, teachers, staff, and the Benedictine community as they face the difficult transition.

Glenstal Abbey announced it would wind down operations no later than August 2028 after 94 years of providing secondary education to boys aged 12 to 18 since 1932. In their statement, the Abbey noted that the decision was not made suddenly or lightly, and that they had wrestled with the school's future for years amid a significantly changed operating environment.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.localAngle: The closure affects a long-standing Limerick educational institution that has served the local community for nearly a century, prompting support from neighbouring schools across the city.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.originalTitle: Limerick schools show support following shock Glenstal Abbey announcement

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.headline: Dr Hammad Danish Appointed as New Respiratory Consultant at UHL
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.summary: University Hospital Limerick has appointed Dr Hammad Danish as its new Consultant Respiratory Physician. He brings expertise in bronchoscopy, pleural procedures, and non-invasive ventilation to the Mid West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.story:
University Hospital Limerick (UHL) has welcomed Dr Hammad Danish as its newest Consultant Respiratory Physician. Hospital officials said his specialist background will significantly boost respiratory healthcare services for patients throughout the Mid West.

Dr Danish's clinical expertise covers advanced procedures including bronchoscopy and pleural interventions, alongside specialized care for patients who require non-invasive ventilation.

Speaking on his appointment, Dr Danish expressed enthusiasm for his new role at the Limerick facility. He stated he is looking forward to working with the local team to advance respiratory services, ensure timely diagnoses and treatments, and improve overall outcomes for patients managing various respiratory conditions across the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.localAngle: The appointment directly strengthens specialized respiratory healthcare services for patients across Limerick and the wider Mid West region at University Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.originalTitle: New Respiratory consultant appointed at UHL

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.headline: Limerick Council Trials Zero Gravity Machine to Boost Biodiversity and Cut Emissions
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.summary: Limerick City and County Council successfully trialled a GHS Drive 1800 zero gravity machine to cut and collect meadow vegetation. The local authority is now exploring purchasing the low-emission equipment permanently.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.story:
Limerick City and County Council has successfully completed a trial of a zero gravity machine designed to enhance biodiversity management and support local climate action objectives across the county.

Leased for a trial period, the GHS Drive 1800 was used to cut and collect vegetation from grasslands and pollinator-friendly meadows within the Limerick Decarbonisation Zone and surrounding areas. Unlike traditional mowing methods, the machine cuts and removes vegetation in a single operation. This removal process is recognized as a best-practice technique that creates conditions for native wildflowers and pollinators to thrive.

The pilot program delivered several environmental and operational benefits, including reduced fuel consumption, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and less noise compared to conventional management methods. According to research, well-managed wildflower meadows encourage deeper root systems and increased soil carbon storage, transforming grasslands into valuable carbon sinks.

Following the success of the trial, Limerick City and County Council intends to explore purchasing a similar machine to support its long-term approach to sustainable grassland management and climate action, aligning with the Limerick Biodiversity Action Plan, the Climate Action Plan, and the All-Ireland Pollinator Plan.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.localAngle: The trial directly impacts local green spaces and decarbonisation efforts within Limerick City and County Council's jurisdiction.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.originalTitle: Zero gravity machine hitting heights in biodiversity

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.headline: Councillors Clash Over Plan to Transfer Six Abbeyfeale Properties to Limerick Twenty Thirty
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.summary: Local representatives have raised serious concerns after Mayor John Moran proposed handing over six council-owned properties in Abbeyfeale to project development company Limerick Twenty Thirty for a cost-recovery rental model.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.story:
Elected members in the Newcastle West district have warned the local authority that it risks "creating a monster" following proposals to dispose of six Council-owned properties in Abbeyfeale to Limerick Twenty Thirty Strategic Development DAC. The plan, tied to Mayor John Moran’s mayoral programme, aims to use the properties to provide a cost-recovery rental model for working households and key workers in the West Limerick town.

The properties involved include sites at Convent Road, 6 and 7 Colbert Terrace, 8 Old Church Street, and units 1 and 2 at the Bridge Inn, comprising a mix of one, two, three, and four-bed units. According to the Council, the intervention is designed to diversify the local housing offer, strengthen local spending power, and support long-term economic sustainability.

However, Fianna Fáil councillor Michael Collins strongly objected to the move during October’s district meeting, arguing that Limerick Twenty Thirty should focus on commercial developments rather than private housing matters. Cllr Collins called for an immediate workshop for all elected members and criticized a private meeting held between the Mayor and district Cathaoirleach Cllr Liam Galvin regarding the properties.

Cllr Galvin defended his involvement, explaining that the houses had been lying idle for two years and are now finished to a "Grade A standard" ready for mid-November. While noting he had initial reservations about the Mayor's proposed scheme, Cllr Galvin stated he is willing to give the initiative a chance to address community concerns over the vacant stock.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.localAngle: The dispute highlights ongoing debates among Limerick councillors over the division of commercial and private housing remits in county towns like Abbeyfeale.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.originalTitle: Proposed disposal of Abbeyfeale properties to Limerick Twenty Thirty raises serious questions

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.headline: Limerick Property Prices Rise by €10,000 to Reach Median Asking Price of €290,000
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.summary: Property prices across Limerick have increased by €10,000 over the past year, bringing the median asking price to €290,000 according to the latest Q3 report. While overall prices remained flat over the quarter, availability grew with 444 properties listed for sale.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.story:
Property prices in Limerick have climbed by €10,000 over the past year, bringing the median asking price for a home in the county to €290,000, according to the latest MyHome Property Price Report for the third quarter of 2026. While overall prices held steady over the quarter, the figures show varying trends across different housing types. Asking prices for three-bed semi-detached houses rose by €15,000 over the year to reach €295,000, marking a €5,000 increase in the last quarter alone. In contrast, four-bed semi-detached homes saw a yearly decrease of €5,500 to €359,500, despite experiencing a €7,000 quarterly rise.

Market availability improved locally, with 444 properties listed for sale across Limerick at the end of the third quarter, representing a 4 per cent increase over the period. Homes in the county are currently taking an average of just under three months to go sale agreed.

Commenting on the wider findings, Bank of Ireland Chief Economist Conall MacCoille said the report offers positive news for prospective buyers. "The rate of asking price inflation continues to slow, the number of properties for sale on MyHome is rising, and homebuilding has picked up. All of these factors point to positive news for homebuyers," he said. Nationally, MyHome Managing Director Joanne Geary noted a continued discrepancy between the first-time buyer and mover markets, with first-time buyer transactions up 12 per cent year-on-year while mover transactions fell slightly by 1.2 per cent.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.localAngle: The latest housing report details specific asking price trends and inventory levels for homes across Limerick city and county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.originalTitle: Limerick property prices continue to rise according to new report

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.headline: Big Shots Halloween Screams Film Competition Returns to Belltable on October 31
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.summary: Ireland’s All-Island Horror Film Competition is bringing its live screening, awards, and cash prizes to the Belltable on Saturday, October 31. Tickets for the Halloween night event cost €12.50, with doors opening at 6.30pm.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.story:
Horror filmmakers from across Ireland are gearing up for the return of Big Shots Halloween Screams to the Belltable on Saturday, October 31. Throughout the month of October, competing teams have been writing, shooting, and editing original short horror films to be showcased on the big screen.

The event, which follows previous successful editions in Limerick in 2024 and 2025, invites a live audience to view the finished entries. Attendees will also see various awards and cash prizes handed out to the standout productions of the night.

Doors at the O'Connell Street venue will open at 6.30pm ahead of the screenings, which are scheduled to kick off at 7.30pm. Tickets for the Halloween film event are priced at €12.50.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.localAngle: The annual horror film showcase returns to Limerick's Belltable venue, offering local film fans a live screening of original short movies on Halloween night.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.originalTitle: Big Shots Halloween Screams returns to Belltable for another night of frights

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.headline: Young Curators bring LASTA '26 festival to Belltable with film and variety show
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.summary: Co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca are bringing the youth-led LASTA '26 festival to Limerick's Belltable later this month, featuring a classic film screening and a multi-act variety show.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.story:
The Belltable is set to host two distinct events this month as part of LASTA ‘26, a national mentorship programme festival showcasing work made for and by young people. Co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca have put together the local programme to open up the venue as a space for creative experimentation and fun for their peers.

The festival opens on Wednesday, October 28, with screenings of the 1980 comedy classic 9 to 5 at 5pm and 7.30pm. Presented by Mr Cropper and Ms Luca in tribute to one of its performers, the film stars Dolly Parton, Lily Tomlin, and Jane Fonda as office workers who seek revenge on their sexist boss. Tickets are priced at €8, with concession tickets available for €5.

On Friday, October 30, at 7.30pm, the venue will host Nighttime Medley, a variety show featuring performances by Day Magee, Whimsy, and Limerick-based dance artist Alex Vostokova. The intimate stage show blends performance, drag clowning, and dance, with tickets costing €15 or €10.

Limerick-based artist Alex Vostokova, an Associate Artist at Dance Limerick, will perform Pit, a piece commissioned by CoisCéim Dance Theatre that explores public space and urbanism. The lineup also features Dublin-based artist Day Magee and drag clown performer Whimsy, known for appearances at Electric Picnic and The Outing.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.localAngle: The festival brings youth-led arts programming, including a performance by Limerick-based dance artist Alex Vostokova, directly to the Belltable stage.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.originalTitle: Young curators bring LASTA ‘26 to Belltable with film screening and variety show

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.headline: Limerick workers warned casual WhatsApp messages can be used as workplace evidence
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.summary: Local employment experts are warning Limerick workers and managers that informal WhatsApp messages and team chats can be used as official evidence in workplace disputes and investigations. Digital communications connected to colleagues are treated as professional conduct regardless of when or where they are sent.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.story:
Limerick employees and managers are being urged to exercise caution with digital communications as casual WhatsApp messages and team chat tools increasingly become formal workplace evidence. While messaging platforms offer a quick and efficient way to communicate, experts note that informal remarks or jokes sent in haste can look very different when reviewed during a workplace complaint or investigation.

A common issue in local workplace disputes involves screenshots of conversations circulating beyond small groups, highlighting that digital messages are rarely as private as users assume. Conversations that continue outside working hours or blur the line between professional and social topics still fall within the scope of workplace behaviour if they involve colleagues or work matters.

HR Hub, an employment law and human resource management firm based on O'Connell Street in Limerick, advises that employees should operate under the assumption that any message could eventually be seen by a wider audience. Managers carry an additional responsibility, as even informal messages can be interpreted as reflecting organisational views. Organisations are advised to establish clear expectations to ensure professional standards are maintained across all digital platforms.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.localAngle: The guidance was issued by Limerick-based human resource management and employment law experts HR Hub, operating from O’Connell Street.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.originalTitle: Employment Matters: When WhatsApp messages become workplace evidence

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.headline: Met Éireann issues dual weather warnings as Storm Boelo arrives in Limerick
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.summary: Status Yellow rain and wind warnings are in effect for Limerick as Storm Boelo brings heavy downpours and severe gusts. The county faces difficult travel conditions and possible structural damage.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.story:
Limerick is bracing for severe weather as Storm Boelo hits the county in the early hours of Saturday morning. Met Éireann has issued consecutive Status Yellow alerts for both rain and wind, warning locals of difficult travelling conditions, localized flooding, and potential disruption to outdoor events.

The rain warning takes effect at 4am on Saturday and runs until 3pm, to be immediately followed by a Status Yellow wind warning starting at 1pm and lasting until noon on Sunday. Forecasters have cautioned that severe and damaging gusts could cause structural damage to homes and businesses, alongside widespread delays to public transport.

Speaking on RTÉ’s Morning Ireland, Met Éireann senior forecaster Gerry Murphy noted that Storm Boelo differs in trajectory from Storm Austen, which passed over the country last Thursday. Heavy rain is expected to develop in the west after midnight and quickly sweep across the country, bringing wet and windy conditions throughout the weekend.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.localAngle: Limerick residents face hazardous travel and potential property damage as Status Yellow wind and rain warnings blanket the county for the weekend.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.originalTitle: Storm Boelo set to hit Limerick with high winds and heavy rain

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.headline: Limerick Chamber reveals shortlist for 15th annual Regional Business Awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.summary: Limerick Chamber has announced the finalists for its 15th annual Regional Business Awards, sponsored by TUS. Winners will be revealed at a gala dinner on November 13 at the Limerick Strand Hotel.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.story:
The finalists for the 15th annual Limerick Chamber Regional Business Awards have officially been named. Sponsored by the Technological University of the Shannon (TUS), the awards celebrate businesses across the Mid-West region ranging from emerging enterprises to established companies.

Limerick Chamber President Maria Gleeson praised the shortlisted organisations for their contributions to the region's success. "What stands out each year is the breadth of talent and enterprise across the Mid-West," she said. Liam Brown, Vice President at TUS, added that the awards provide an important platform to recognise the organisations shaping the future of the local economy.

The shortlist features competitive categories including Best Emerging Business, Best SME, Best Employer, Community Impact, Environmental Excellence, Customer Experience, Innovation and Digital Transformation, and Best Not-for-Profit Impact. Nominees include local names such as Fíor Jewellery, Croom Medical, Mother Macs, and the University Concert Hall.

The winners will be announced on Friday, November 13, at a gala dinner held at the Limerick Strand Hotel, attended by senior leaders from across the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.localAngle: The awards celebrate local businesses and enterprises driving economic and community success across Limerick and the wider Mid-West region.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.headline: Limerick Magician Steve Spade Channels Harry Houdini at Bunratty Castle Halloween Event
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.summary: Limerick master magician Steve Spade is headlining the bank holiday Halloween event at Bunratty Castle and Folk Park this weekend, recreating famous escapes exactly one century after Harry Houdini's passing.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.story:
Limerick master magician Steve Spade is bringing his homage to Harry Houdini to Bunratty Castle and Folk Park this bank holiday weekend, marking the centenary of the legendary escapologist's death. Spade, often called the Irish Houdini, owns a set of Houdini's own handcuffs after winning a rope-tie challenge on the Discovery Channel programme 'Baggage Battles'.

Speaking about his three-day appearance at the Co Clare venue, Spade confirmed he will perform live escapes alongside traditional parlour magic and host a question-and-answer session on Houdini's life and career. The Limerick magician's appearance is part of a broader commemoration, which also includes a private seance at Limerick's Studio Saol.

Visitors to Bunratty over the Halloween weekend will also encounter a range of spooky attractions, including the Human Spider illusion, Vera the Velociraptor, a Ghost Recruitment Bureau, a Wicked Wake, and a lively Witch Trial. Families can additionally enjoy apple bobbing in the Golden Vale and performances by international contortionist and juggler Frederico Fandango.

Spade's performances bridge local talent with international magic history, offering Limerick families a high-profile attraction just across the county border for the bank holiday weekend.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.localAngle: Limerick master magician Steve Spade is starring in the Bunratty Castle Halloween event, bringing his internationally recognised talents and Houdini memorabilia to a local audience.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.originalTitle: Spirit of Houdini will be one of the friendly ghosts to haunt Bunratty this weekend

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.headline: Limerick Psychotherapist Warns CORU Fast-Track Training Puts Vulnerable at Risk
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.summary: Limerick psychotherapist Trish Murphy has warned that CORU's proposed fast-track training regulations could fail vulnerable people. The Irish Council for Psychotherapy argues the changes dilute standards by cutting supervision and personal therapy requirements.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.story:
A Limerick psychotherapist has warned that proposed new training regulations aimed at clearing mental health waiting lists could put vulnerable people at risk. Trish Murphy, a Limerick native and Director of Student Counselling Services at Trinity College Dublin, issued the warning following her organisation's annual conference.

Ms Murphy echoed concerns raised by the Irish Council for Psychotherapy (ICP) regarding new standards of proficiency suggested by health professionals regulatory body CORU. The proposed changes would introduce a shorter training period while dropping requirements for personal therapy and supervision, alongside a reduced focus on the therapeutic relationship.

"Newly trained psychotherapists will not be equipped to provide the relational capacity that is essential to the long-term processing of trauma when treating the most vulnerable children, adolescents, and adult clients," Ms Murphy said.

Rúaidhrí O’Connor, CEO of the ICP, criticized the regulatory body for failing to consult directly with professional representative bodies between December 2023 and July 2025. The ICP is urging CORU to engage with the profession to ensure public protection remains central to regulatory decisions.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.localAngle: The warning was issued by Limerick-native Trish Murphy, a qualified psychotherapist and Director of Student Counselling Services at Trinity College Dublin, following her organization's annual conference.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.originalTitle: Limerick psychotherapist warns of dangers of fast-track training
